l.i: Nomina in us quomodo habent in Vocativo?

main_text.l: Nomina Appellativa vel Propria secūdæ declina-
tionis in us,habēt in Vocativo e: ut,Dominus,domi-
ne. Tabellarius,tabellarie. Fluvius,fluvie,& fluvius
per Antiptosin. Sic Agnus, Chorus populus e & us
habere creduntur.Tria appellativa definūt in i: ut,Fi-
lius, fili, ein sohn. Meus,mi,mein. Genius, genii,ein
Gott oder Engel der natur. Deus, & Lucus,ein
geweihter wald/Vocativo manent.At Oedipus,ōOedi-
pu. Propria in ius vel jus abjiciunt in Vocativo us,

page.notes: The first line starts with a Fraktur "und" and a Fraktur "klein" (the k is hard to read, so "klein" is taken from context). Several German words are in black letter and are marked with <bl>; the marking is my reading and may be wrong for some words. "stulgang" and "Methodus" are read with some doubt. The Greek "ὕσσωπος" after Hyssopus is partly illegible in the scan. "Vannus,ein wann" is copied as printed; the word may be a misprint for "mann". "Crystallstein" and "zwenfal-" are printed this way. The heading "Nomina in us quomodo habent in Vocativo?" is in italics; I took it as a level-2 heading.
